description: The plot illustrates the relationship between “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” on the x-axis and “Accuracy” on the y-axis, comparing two metrics: “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and error bars) and “Final Accuracy” (blue dashed line with circle markers and error bars). The x-axis ranges from 1 to 19 in increments of 2, representing o_pop frequency scaled by 10^4, and is linearly spaced. The y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, representing accuracy as a unitless proportion. The green “Initial Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.35 at x=1, rises to ~0.5 at x=5, dips to ~0.3 at x=7, peaks again at ~0.55 at x=13, then declines to ~0.35 at x=17 before rising slightly to ~0.4 at x=19. The blue “Final Accuracy” line starts at ~0.65 at x=1, increases to ~0.85 at x=5, dips to ~0.7 at x=7, peaks at ~0.95 at x=9, drops to ~0.7 at x=11, rises to ~0.9 at x=15, dips to ~0.8 at x=17, and ends at ~0.9 at x=19. Error bars are present for both lines, indicating variability, and are generally larger for “Final Accuracy” than for “Initial Accuracy” across most x-values.
